name: Business-Airport Kyobashi
card: The charm of a craftsmen's district, in a gentle Japanese style
title: Business-Airport Kyobashi — a workplace expressing a district of makers in Japanese style, at FPG links KYOBASHI
lead: Business-Airport Kyobashi, run by Tokyu Land, is on the 2nd and 4th–8th floors of FPG links KYOBASHI in Kyobashi 2-chome. Kyobashi was a “town of making” where Edo-period creators honed their craft side by side, and the website describes a space that expresses the charm of that craftsmen's district with a gentle Japanese touch. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Serviced offices (private) / coworking / meeting rooms A, B, C / online meeting room
concept: Opening up a new era in Kyobashi, the town of making
The slogan is “Opening up a new era in Kyobashi, the town of making”. Kyobashi is where Edo-period creators competed and improved, and today it is a major business district.
The website describes a space that expresses the charm of that craftsmen's town in a gentle Japanese style — a workplace that stirs the creativity of business people and creators alike.
steps: Address membership is ¥71,500 a month, Master ¥38,500, Private ¥14,300, and Flex ¥550 per 30 minutes.
Private rooms for one start at ¥165,000 a month; rooms for several people from ¥253,000.
Serviced offices can be entered 24 hours a day.
Room A seats eight at ¥3,300 an hour, room B four at ¥2,200 and room C six at ¥2,750.
The one-person online meeting room costs ¥550 per 30 minutes.

word.title: What does “Japanese style” mean here?
body: A design atmosphere that draws on traditional Japanese materials, forms and colours. Business-Airport Kyobashi uses it gently to express the charm of a craftsmen's district.
Bringing Japanese elements into an office building softens its hard edges.

name: Business-Airport Shibuya Fukuras
card: High up on the 17th floor of Shibuya Fukuras, in front of Shibuya Station
title: Business-Airport Shibuya Fukuras — a high-rise workplace on the 17th floor of Shibuya Fukuras, in front of the station
lead: Business-Airport Shibuya Fukuras, run by Tokyu Land, is on the 17th floor of Shibuya Fukuras in front of Shibuya Station. It has private rooms, coworking, meeting rooms and an event space for 20, and the serviced offices are open 24 hours. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Serviced offices (private) / coworking / meeting rooms A, B / online meeting room / event space
Coworking weekdays 7:00–22:00, Sundays and holidays 10:00–18:00 (closed Saturdays) / serviced offices 24 hours
concept: On the 17th floor, in front of Shibuya Station
Business-Airport Shibuya Fukuras is on the 17th floor of Shibuya Fukuras, right in front of Shibuya Station.
Business-Airport is Tokyu Land's brand, named after an airport where diverse people gather and depart. In Shibuya it also has the Shibuya Sakura Stage and Shibuya Nanpeidai sites.
steps: From 7:00 on weekdays, and open on Sundays and holidays
Coworking is open 7:00–22:00 on weekdays (reception 9:00–18:00) and 10:00–18:00 on Sundays and holidays. It is closed on Saturdays.
Address membership is ¥99,000 a month, Master ¥38,500, Private ¥14,300, and Flex ¥550 per 30 minutes.
Rooms for one, and for 2–5 people
Private rooms for one cost ¥198,000 a month; rooms for 2–5 start at ¥363,000.
Serviced offices can be entered 24 hours a day.
Two rooms for six, and an event space for 20
Meeting rooms A and B seat six at ¥2,750 an hour; the one-person online meeting room is ¥550 per 30 minutes.
The event space holds 20 people: ¥33,000 an hour for members and ¥49,500 for non-members.

word.title: What is Master membership?
body: A Business-Airport membership that lets you use the coworking areas of every site, for ¥38,500 a month.
With three sites in Shibuya alone, you can pick the one that fits your schedule that day.

name: Business-Airport Shibuya Nanpeidai
card: Shibuya, city of entertainment — from here to the world
title: Business-Airport Shibuya Nanpeidai — from the city of entertainment to the world, on the 3rd floor of SHIBUYA SOLASTA
lead: Business-Airport Shibuya Nanpeidai, run by Tokyu Land, is on the 3rd floor of SHIBUYA SOLASTA in Dogenzaka 1-chome. Under the slogan “Shibuya, city of entertainment. From here to the world”, it is a base for forward-looking startups and companies drawn by Shibuya's entertainment and originality. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: ROOM / BOOTH / DESK / shared workspace / 3 meeting rooms
Coworking weekdays 7:00–22:00, Saturdays 10:00–18:00 / serviced offices 24 hours
concept: Shibuya, city of entertainment — from here to the world
The website writes: “Shibuya, city of entertainment. From here to the world. Shibuya's entertainment and originality captivate people and attract forward-looking startups and companies.”
Nanpeidai is a quiet area a little uphill from Shibuya Station. On the 3rd floor of SHIBUYA SOLASTA are private rooms, booths, fixed desks and a shared workspace.
steps: From 7:00 on weekdays, and open on Saturdays
The shared workspace is open 7:00–22:00 on weekdays (reception 9:00–18:00) and 10:00–18:00 on Saturdays.
Address membership is ¥82,500 a month, Master ¥38,500, Private ¥14,300, and Flex ¥550 per 30 minutes.
Private ROOMs start at ¥165,000 a month, BOOTHs at ¥132,000 and fixed DESKs at ¥104,500.
Serviced offices can be entered 24 hours a day.
Two rooms for eight and one for four
Meeting rooms 1 and 2 seat eight at ¥3,300 an hour; room 3 seats four at ¥2,200.
The one-person online meeting room costs ¥550 per 30 minutes.

word.title: Where is Nanpeidai?
body: The name of the area west of Shibuya Station, at the top of the Dogenzaka slope — a calm spot a little away from the bustle around the station.
Championing Shibuya's entertainment while sitting in quiet Nanpeidai: keeping the right distance between stimulation and calm is this site's character.

name: WORK STYLING Tokyo Midtown Hibiya
card: “ZEN MODERN” on the 12th floor, decorated with traditional Japanese patterns
title: WORK STYLING Tokyo Midtown Hibiya — a “ZEN MODERN” shared office with traditional patterns, on the 12th floor of Hibiya Mitsui Tower
lead: Mitsui Fudosan's WORK STYLING Tokyo Midtown Hibiya is on the 12th floor of Hibiya Mitsui Tower. Its design concept is “ZEN MODERN”: a space decorated with traditional Japanese patterns, with an open space, meeting rooms for up to 12, single-person private rooms and rental offices. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Open space / meeting rooms (up to 12) / single-person rooms / rental offices
concept: ZEN MODERN
The design concept of WORK STYLING Tokyo Midtown Hibiya is “ZEN MODERN” — a space decorated with traditional Japanese patterns, according to the website.

WORK STYLING is Mitsui Fudosan's office service. The Hibiya site is on the 12th floor of Hibiya Mitsui Tower at Tokyo Midtown Hibiya; SHARE (shared office) is open 8:00–21:00 on weekdays, and FLEX members can enter 24 hours.
steps: Meeting rooms hold up to 12 people, and each is a different size so you can choose by the number of attendees.
In the heart of Hibiya, they are handy for meetings with visitors.
Rooms to shut the door and focus
Single-person rooms are for calls, online meetings and focused work.
There are also rental offices you can take as a team base.

word.title: What is ZEN MODERN?
body: The design concept of WORK STYLING Tokyo Midtown Hibiya. Traditional Japanese patterns overlay the calm of Zen on today's way of working.
In Hibiya, a district with many visitors from overseas, it is a choice to convey Japaneseness through the interior.

credits: WORK STYLING official website: “Tokyo Midtown Hibiya (SHARE + FLEX)”

name: DIAGONAL RUN TOKYO
card: Where Tokyo and the regions — people, companies and ideas — cross diagonally
title: DIAGONAL RUN TOKYO — coworking linking Tokyo with the rest of Japan, on the 4th floor of Kyobashi MID Building
lead: DIAGONAL RUN TOKYO is on the 4th floor of the Kyobashi MID Building, about a minute's walk from Takaracho Station on the Toei Asakusa Line. It is a coworking space where Tokyo meets regions across Japan, and where people, companies (technologies), ideas and information intersect. It has free desks, booths, small offices, meeting rooms and an event space. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Drop-in / free desk / booth / small office / meeting room / event space
About 1 min from Takaracho Sta. / about 3 min from Kyobashi Sta. / about 11 min from Tokyo Sta.
concept: Where Tokyo meets the rest of Japan

DIAGONAL RUN TOKYO aims to be a place where Tokyo and regions across Japan — and people, companies (technologies), ideas and information — meet. The word “diagonal” suggests connections that cut across the usual vertical and horizontal lines.
On the 4th floor of the Kyobashi MID Building, within walking distance of Tokyo Station, it is a gateway where people arriving from the regions meet people working in Tokyo.
steps: Drop-in is ¥3,300 a day, or from ¥660 an hour on weekdays.
Free desks start at ¥18,700 a month.
Seats for one, rooms for teams
Booths start at ¥48,400 a month and small offices at ¥148,500.
You can move from a free desk to a booth to a small office as your team grows.
Meeting rooms from 30 minutes, and a place for events
Meeting rooms start at ¥2,200 per 30 minutes, and the event space at ¥55,000 an hour.
It is the stage for events linking regions across Japan with Tokyo.

word.title: Why “diagonal”?
body: The English word that gives DIAGONAL RUN TOKYO its name.
Against vertical organisations and horizontal industries, it cuts across at an angle — a name for a place that links Tokyo and the regions, people, companies and ideas diagonally.

name: BIRTH WORK Kanda
card: Private rooms facing the windows, and a workspace with a view
title: BIRTH WORK Kanda — a “grow-with-you” flexible office on the 4th, 6th and 7th floors of the Kanda Takagi Building
lead: BIRTH WORK Kanda is in the Kanda Takagi Building in Kanda-Nishikicho 1-chome. It aims “to promote company growth as Japan's first ‘growth-type free-working office’”, with private rooms for 3–8 people on the 4th and 7th floors and a workspace with a view on the 6th. It can be entered 24 hours a day. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: 4F four private rooms / 6F workspace / 7F three private rooms and lounge
concept: A growth-type free-working office

BIRTH WORK Kanda aims “to promote company growth as Japan's first ‘growth-type free-working office’”. From a workspace for one to private rooms for 3–8 people, companies can move rooms within the same building as they grow.
BIRTH is Takagi Building's brand, with sites in Azabu-Juban and Toranomon as well. In Kanda it uses three floors: the 4th, 6th and 7th.
steps: Window seats with a view, and sofa seats
The 6th floor is the workspace, with “window seats with a good view and comfortable sofa seats”, the website says.
It can be booked out for events of about 30 people. Free working costs ¥27,500 a month and the BIRTHERs plan ¥38,500.
Four bright rooms facing the windows
The 4th floor has four private rooms for 3–8 people, all bright offices facing the windows.
Private rooms cost ¥104,500 to ¥231,000 a month.
Three private rooms and a lounge-style shared area
The 7th floor has three private rooms for 3–8 people, and the shared area is set up as a lounge.
Teams working in private rooms can take a break in the shared lounge.

word.title: What is a growth-type free-working office?
body: BIRTH WORK Kanda's own term: start at a workspace on your own, then move into private rooms in the same building as the company grows.
Growing without moving is a big advantage for a small company.

credits: BIRTH WORK Kanda (Takagi Building Co., Ltd.)

name: BIRTH WORK Toranomon
card: A second office in warm wood, like a study at home
title: BIRTH WORK Toranomon — a wood-toned second office divided into study-like spaces, in Nishi-Shimbashi 1-chome
lead: BIRTH WORK Toranomon is in Nishi-Shimbashi 1-chome. Billed as “a second office just like a study at home”, it divides its floors into a focus zone on the 2nd floor and a meeting and relaxation zone on the 3rd. The 2nd floor is a working office in warm wood, split into small sections to create a space where you can focus for four hours straight. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: 2F focus zone / 3F meeting and relaxation zone
24-hour access (open every day except building inspections)
concept: A second office, just like a study at home
BIRTH WORK Toranomon calls itself “a second office just like a study at home” — a second workplace, neither company office nor home, for calm thinking.
The 2nd floor is for focus and the 3rd for meetings and relaxing. You move between the two floors, each with its own role, by the stairs.
steps: A wood-toned office divided into small sections
The 2nd floor is “a working office in warm wood, divided into small sections to create a space where you can concentrate for four hours”.
Dividing a large room into small ones lets each person work as if shut away in their own study.
A private meeting room for up to six
The 3rd floor has a private meeting room for up to six people and a space for face-to-face discussions.
After focused work, you move upstairs to talk or rest.
A virtual plan; free working currently closed to new members
The virtual plan costs ¥5,500 a month (sign-up fee ¥16,500). The official website says free working is not currently accepting new members.
It can be entered 24 hours a day and is open every day (except for building inspections).

word.title: What is a second office?
body: A second place to work, separate from the company office and from home. BIRTH WORK Toranomon offers one “like a study at home”.
Finding the quiet that neither office nor home can give, in a second place — the word “study” captures its character well.

credits: BIRTH WORK Toranomon (Takagi Building Co., Ltd.)

name: Business-Airport Kanda
card: Retro design sprinkled with new trends
title: Business-Airport Kanda — a workplace sprinkling new trends over a retro style, on the 7th floor of oak Kanda Kajicho
lead: Business-Airport Kanda, run by Tokyu Land, is on the 7th floor of oak Kanda Kajicho in Kanda-Kajicho 3-chome. The website describes a workplace that blends new trends seamlessly into a retro design style, giving a curious sense of calm and comfort. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: ROOM / BOOTH / coworking / meeting room / online meeting room
Coworking weekdays 8:00–20:00, Saturdays 10:00–18:00 / serviced offices 24 hours
concept: New trends in a retro style
The website describes “a workplace that sprinkles new trends naturally over a retro design style, with a curious calm and comfort”.
Kanda is a district where old-established trade and new companies mix. The interior expresses that character by blending old and new.
steps: From 8:00 on weekdays, and open on Saturdays
Coworking is open 8:00–20:00 on weekdays (reception 9:00–18:00) and 10:00–18:00 on Saturdays.
Address membership is ¥71,500 a month, Master ¥38,500, Private ¥14,300, and Flex ¥550 per 30 minutes.
Private ROOMs start at ¥275,000 a month and BOOTHs at ¥110,000.
Serviced offices can be entered 24 hours a day.
The meeting room seats eight at ¥3,300 an hour; the one-person online meeting room is ¥550 per 30 minutes.
Meet in a calm, retro setting.

word.title: What does retro mean here?
body: Design that evokes the styles and mood of the past and enjoys their flavour. Business-Airport Kanda sprinkles new trends over a retro style.
Bringing an old-time atmosphere into a new building creates a sense of calm.
